system.summary: The second Höpken-Carlson code (as in hopken1740): four-digit groups seen between 1006 and 1915, a syllabary built for Swedish (i/j, u/v/w, a/å/ä, o/ö not distinguished) with word codes for names and terms (1287 storviziren = Grand Vizir, 1713 grefwen = comte, 1516 ottporten = Porte, 1511 hof = Cour, 1448 fred = paix, 1360 tractat = traité). Used here for French; a stroke over a group marks an accent or an apostrophe (1006' = d', 1251' = dé, 1500' = à).
system.notes: Seed values read by eye only in the first build; the key was then rebuilt from the glossed despatch (235 confirmed values) and extended by 24 values from Lit. A's gloss. Key: key.tsv of this folder (as on origin/main 54c4ecc65), applied frozen and unchanged; key_1741.tsv adds 24 values read from the Lit. A gloss and corrects two single values of it (1504 vo, 1840 au).

prior_solution.where: The contemporary Swedish decipherment written over the groups on images 322-327. No edition or modern decipherment found (web searches, 10 Nov 2026). For the 1741 pages: the contemporary French gloss over Lit. A (image 147); the Castellane letter and the reply have none. Castellane's own letters of 1740-47 are in the French diplomatic archives (Nantes), not checked.

conditions.human_role: Daniel Bourdeau set the task for the despatch of 1740; WAINUT set the task for the 1741 pages (catalogue 2245-2248) and the rules; AI language-model agents transcribed, froze and applied the key, ran the held-out test, read and checked. No human palaeographer checked the text.

solution.what: Images 322-327 of R0003582 fetched from the Riksarkivet IIIF service at full size.
Pass 1 by two AI agents with the Swedish gloss in view: 123 runs, 2118 groups (pairs_322_324.tsv, pairs_325_327.tsv); 23 runs K. Gloss column rough and loosely aligned.
Groups above 1749 (to about 1999) and value clashes with the French-glossed code of 255-261 show a second code; split from hopken1739.
Hard-EM segmentation on the 23 K runs with 9 seeds: alignments are not usable (gloss extents too loose). Word-level re-pairing started.
Word-level pairs re-read from full-size crops by three agents (wordpairs_*.tsv): gloss word, groups under it, segmentation; 2,119 groups.
Key from the K lines of 322-325 frozen (key_frozen_322_325.tsv): 147 confirmed, 15 mixed, 67 single.

Held-out test on 326-327: 457 of 598 groups give exactly the piece of the pairing (522 in key); shuffled-key control mean 3.5, max 33 of 500. Not strictly blind: the 326-327 agent had seeds.tsv and could have seen the 324-325 pairs. Rerun after the recheck of doubtful lines (more K lines on 326-327): 525 of 687.

Recheck of the 94 doubtful lines with the full key: 63 settled, 31 remain. Final key 190 confirmed / 23 mixed / 87 single. 2,027 of 2,119 groups (95.7%) in confident words. Swedish reading and English translation written.
Images 319-321 and 328-342 fetched: the despatch is No. 2 of 15/26 Jan 1740, images 321-331; images 332-342 are a second copy in the same encipherment (332-333 glossed, 334-342 bare).
Word-level pairs for 321 and 328-331 by two agents with key.tsv in view (1,331 groups).

Bare second copy transcribed digits-only by three agents told to open no other file: 3,082 groups, 2,987 identical in sequence to the glossed copy. 116 digits taken from the bare copy at one-for-one differences (scripts/apply_bare.py).

Second recheck of the 63 doubtful lines against both copies: 51 settled, 11 remain. Final key 235 confirmed / 15 mixed / 78 single; 3,411 of 3,450 groups (98.9%) in confident words. Reading and translation extended to the whole despatch.

Images named by catalogue 2245-2248 fetched at 1200 px from four volumes (R0003590, R0003628, R0003635, R0003636) for contact sheets; R0003636 images 49-51 and R0003635 image 147 at full size; one at a time, 1.6 s apart, no block.
Image 147: 18 cipher rows, two passes, digits only; gloss read onto gloss_lita_1741.tsv afterwards.

Held-out test of the hopken1740 key (frozen unchanged from origin/main; built on volume I/9/21 from a Swedish gloss) against the gloss of the French Lit. A page (R0003635_00147): 222 of 282 groups (79%) give exactly the letters of the gloss at their place, 92% of the 242 groups in the key; shuffled-key control mean 33.4, maximum 51 over 200 shuffles (scripts/heldout.py).
24 new values and 2 corrections read from the gloss (key.tsv, status gloss_1741a / changed_1741a).

Reading built from the cipher with key.tsv; four places where the cipher differs from the gloss noted (de paix, y couvre, auquel, les articles du dit). Marked form against the frozen key checked by scripts/check_marks.py: 84 of 122 words verbatim from the frozen key, 3 repaired, 35 resting on values read from the gloss. Dan's checker: clean share 0.909 (10 of 11 sentences).

Blind review by an independent AI language-model agent: 92 groups read from its own crops before opening the transcriptions (23 on image 147), no disagreement; the key applied frozen is byte-identical to origin/main targets/hopken1740/key.tsv; decrypt.py, check_marks.py and heldout.py rerun and reproduced. State read, grade A. One fix: the translation now notes that the cipher has 'couvre' for 'découvre'.
Image 49 (whole page) and image 50 (left page) transcribed in two passes; 5 disagreements settled or kept doubtful.
this folder's key.tsv applied frozen and unchanged; key_1741.tsv adds 24 values read from the Lit. A gloss and corrects 1504 and 1840.

Mechanical decryption with key.tsv read as French, every departure marked; scripts/check_marks.py passes. Castellane letter: 79 of 94 words verbatim, 2 repaired, 13 guessed, 0 holes. Reply: 109 of 123 verbatim, 3 repaired, 10 guessed, 1 hole (after the review fix below). Dan's checker: clean share 0.444 (letter, 4 of 9 sentences) and 0.615 (reply, 8 of 13); it counts each context-guessed word as a hole.

Integration check (12 Nov 2026): the key_frozen.tsv of both 1741 folders is byte-identical to this folder's key.tsv (sha256 c4e208fe...8ef1ac), so the two folders were folded into hopken1740 (one key, one entry). heldout.py reproduced (222 of 282 groups, 242 in key; shuffled-key control mean 33.4, max 51 over 200); check_marks.py passes for Lit. A, the letter and the reply; make_key_1741.py rebuilds key_1741.tsv; an own decoder gives the same mechanical text of the Castellane letter. Images R0003636_00049 (all rows of the letter, the reply heading) and R0003635_00147 rows H04-H08 fetched from lbiiif.riksarkivet.se and compared: no disagreement at that reading. The bare pages were read with key_1741.tsv (frozen key + 24 gloss values + 2 corrections): letter 180 of 205 groups in the frozen key, 191 in key_1741; reply 245 of 269 and 258. The eight values proposed from the sense before the gloss were not frozen in a file (contributor's record). Strict share of the bare pages 188 of 217 words (86.6%).

Statistical validation (docs/_validate.py): 449 tokens, 125 types, fr-1600-letters order 4: reading -1.952 per letter; random keys -3.483 (z 12.2); key annealed onto shuffled ciphertext best -2.328 (mean -2.357, z 18.0); annealer on the real text -2.285. Verdict: pass.

Statistical validation (docs/_validate.py) of the two bare documents of 1741 with key_1741.tsv (scripts/validation_pairs_1741.py): 449 read tokens, 125 types, 828 letters, fr-1600-letters order 4: reading -1.952 per letter; random keys -3.483 (z 12.2); key annealed onto shuffled ciphertext best -2.328 (mean -2.357, z 18.0); annealer on the real text -2.285. Verdict: pass. The key was not fitted to these pages (frozen despatch key plus Lit. A's gloss values).

outcome.method: key recovered based on adjacent plaintext
outcome.method_basis: The contemporary Swedish decipherment written over the groups of the despatch of 15/26 Jan 1740 gave the code list (235 confirmed values), frozen and tested on a glossed French page of 1741 (222 of 282 groups, shuffled-key maximum 51); with 24 values and 2 corrections from that page's gloss it reads two bare French documents of 1741, in part.
outcome.fraction_read_source: Strict count by the README read bar over the two bare documents of 1741 (scripts/check_marks.py with key_1741.tsv): words read verbatim from the signs, 79 of 94 (the Castellane letter) and 109 of 123 (the reply to the foot of image 50 left), 188 of 217 = 0.866; guesses, repairs and the one hole are not counted. The glossed documents are the key source and are not counted: the despatch of 1740 (3,411 of 3,450 groups, 98.9%, in confident words) and Lit. A (84 of 122 words from the frozen key, 35 from its gloss, 3 repaired).

The cipher has la-ri-a-[1409]-le; with 1409 = il it gives 'lariaille', so one a serves two words (marked {+a}), or the name is 'Lari'. The reviewer recalls a dragoman family of this name at the French embassy; not checked.

texts.summary: Höpken and Carlson report to the King how the Porte's dragoman brought the signed defensive alliance treaty and asked to delay its exchange and keep it secret, how they argued for a prompt exchange, and how the exemplars were exchanged on 14/25 January 1740 after a present to Ragib Efendi. They credit the King's firmness over the Russian frontier, note the French ambassador's late help, and ask for a provisional instruction and full powers.

reading_review.by: Claude (AI model), reading the Swedish text as sentences while translating it
reading_review.note: Coherent throughout; holes at 11 doubtful words and a few clear words.

texts.label: Lit. A, image 147: memorandum on the last Russo-Ottoman treaty
texts.summary: The more one examines the last peace treaty between the Porte and the Muscovites, the more one finds conditions onerous and unbearable for the Sultan, manifest contradictions, and attempts to deceive the Porte, which the Muscovites treated as an inferior prince on whom they meant to impose laws; this is to be shown article by article, beginning with article 2 on the frontiers (breaks off).
texts.note: Read through the contemporary gloss, checked group by group against the frozen hopken1740 key (79% exact on the gloss, held out). Against the frozen key: 84 of 122 words verbatim, 3 with a marked repair, 35 resting on values read from this gloss. The cipher differs from the gloss in four places, followed in the reading. The page ends mid-sentence; the continuation was not looked for.

reading_review.note: Read as French sentences against the translation: the whole page reads; 84 of 122 words come from the frozen hopken1740 key and the rest from values the contemporary gloss gives over the same groups. 23 groups of this page (92 over the three pages) were spot-checked on the image with no disagreement.

texts.label: Castellane to Höpken and Carlson (cipher copy), image 49 L01-L16
texts.summary: After a general divan at the Porte, the Porte's dragoman invited Castellane on behalf of the Grand Vizier to a kind of congress next Sunday at which Monsieur de Romanzof (probably Rumyantsev, the Russian ambassador) is to be present; he asks the Swedes for their reflections before the sieur de Laria goes to the Porte's dragoman next morning at eight.
texts.note: 94 cipher words: 79 verbatim from the key (84.0%), 2 with a marked repair, 13 resting on context-guessed values, no holes. Every sentence is coherent French; the guessed values are mostly single syllables fixed by the sense, three of them also by recurrence in the reply. In 'le sieur de Laria aille' the cipher writes one a for two (marked {+a}). Checker clean share 0.444, just under 0.45, because it counts each guessed word as a hole.

reading_review.note: Read as French sentences against the translation: all four sentences hold; 13 words rest on syllable values guessed from context and are marked, and none leaves a gap in the sense. Checker share 0.444.

texts.label: Höpken and Carlson to Castellane (cipher copy), image 49 L17 to the foot of image 50 left page
texts.summary: The Swedes thank Castellane for his generous conduct toward the interests of their court, announce a visit next evening to set out their thoughts on Sweden's present interests with regard to Russia and Russia's differences with the Porte, and begin to say that in Sweden's critical situation with Russia any accommodation between the Porte and Russia is ... (breaks off at the foot of the page).
texts.note: 123 cipher words to the foot of the left page of image 50: 109 verbatim (88.6%), 3 repaired, 10 guessed, 1 hole (1515). One clear sentence. Checker clean share 0.615. The text continues on images 50 (right page), 51 and 52, not transcribed.

reading_review.note: Read as French sentences against the translation: the four sentences hold to the break at the foot of the page; one group is unread and 10 words rest on marked context values.
